statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail 10% sits in the low band, well below the block threshold, and the same assessment applies to NQ futures and NAS100 CFD.
recommendation: Tail remains below the block threshold, so the deterministic mapping yields EA_ON for both instruments. Conditional risk is concentrated in the narrow 13:30-15:00 UTC window spanning the US cash open, the S&P Global flash PMIs at 13:45 UTC, the Barr speech at 14:05 UTC and the delayed post-release second leg, where the published forecast reaches the WATCH band for two hours, and again in the 19:00 UTC power hour. Unscheduled headline risk from the Trump-Xi state visit is treated as a Stress and Confidence factor rather than an observed path amplifier. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Overnight range stops extending as NQ holds mid-band, keeping Tail at the low-band floor
body: The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed on 22 September at 30,732.40, up 250.04 points or 0.82 percent, inside a 30,496.43-30,770.63 range and at a fresh 52-week and all-time closing high against a 22,841.42-30,770.63 annual range. Globex NQ now trades at 31,034.50, plus 6.00 points or 0.02 percent, inside the same 30,985.25-31,070.50 overnight band that was in place an hour ago. That band spans 85 points, or roughly 0.27 percent, and the fact that it has not widened over the past hour is the single most informative observation available: price sits about 49 points above the overnight low and about 36 points below the high, which is contained two-way rotation rather than directional efficiency. Cross-asset context is supportive but not uniformly aligned. VIX closed at 14.21, down 0.66 or 4.44 percent, far below the 35.30 top of its annual range. WTI trades near 89.33 dollars, down 1.31 percent, and Brent near 98.47 dollars, down 0.79 percent, extending a sixth consecutive lower session after the restart of Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline and reported diplomatic progress with Iran. Against that, the H.15 curve published on 22 September shows the 2-year at 4.76 percent, the 5-year at 4.83, the 10-year at 4.96 and the 30-year at 5.29, with the 2-year reported as high as 4.7879 percent overnight, its highest since mid-2024, so the valuation cushion under a record-high index is thin. Asia has advanced for a sixth session with MSCI Asia-Pacific ex-Japan up 0.7 percent, Korea up 1.2 percent on Samsung and SK Hynix, and Taiwan up 0.9 percent near record levels, while Tokyo cash is shut for a third consecutive day for the Autumnal Equinox and reopens on 24 September. The day ahead carries European flash PMIs from 07:15 UTC, the S&P Global US flash PMIs at 13:45 UTC just after the cash open, a Fed Governor Barr speech at 14:05 UTC, EIA inventories at 14:30 UTC and a 5-year note auction at 17:00 UTC, while President Xi begins a three-day state visit to Washington whose summit and state dinner fall on 24 September. Those are checkpoints and untimed headline sources, not observed structure, so they raise Stress and shape Confidence without lifting current Tail. Shared Finviz cross-asset context was read but was both stale and flagged partial, so it was excluded and the assessment rests entirely on independently verified primary sources.

lookbackSummary: The last 24 published hours cover one completed US session and its orderly overnight handover. Through the European morning of 22 September Tail sat at 12-13 with Stress in the mid-30s. Tail peaked at 21 in the 14:00 UTC cash-open hour as a trend-up regime established itself, eased to 14-17 across the mixed early afternoon, then returned to 20-21 through the 18:00-19:00 UTC power-hour block ahead of the record close. Since the close Tail has decayed monotonically from 19 to 10 and the dominant mode has reverted from trend-up to normal, which is the decay profile of an orderly advance rather than a path that denied retracement. All 24 slots carry a published assessment and none reached the blocking band.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours run from a thin, holiday-shortened Asian book through the European flash PMI block and into the densest scheduled risk of the day. Tail is held at 11-13 across the Asian and European hours, where the only checkpoints are the French, German, euro-area and UK flash PMIs between 07:15 and 08:30 UTC. It steps to 21-22 for the 13:00 and 14:00 UTC hours, which carry the US cash open, the S&P Global US flash PMIs at 13:45 UTC, the Barr speech at 14:05 UTC and the delayed second-leg window, producing the first WATCH mapping. Tail then decays to 15-17 through the US afternoon around the 17:00 UTC 5-year auction before a secondary rise to 20 in the 19:00 UTC power hour, where a record-close backdrop supports late-session extension. Overnight values return to 11-14, with the Tokyo cash reopen at 00:00 UTC on 24 September the one identifiable structural checkpoint after three closed sessions. Every forecast value beyond the current clock hour is conditional risk, not observed structure, and confidence decays from 88 to 75 across the window.
